title: What if you got stuck in an elevator for 41 hours?
premise: First-person: stuck in an office-tower elevator from Friday night to Sunday afternoon, anchored on the real 41-hour case in New York (1999).

intro.title: What if you got stuck in an elevator for *41 hours*?

lines: Would you climb out, or wait?

beats.caption: You're the last one out. You press the button.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: The doors close. Floor 34, going down.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: Then a jolt.
beats.head: shake

beats.caption: The lights flicker. You're stuck between floors.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: You press the alarm. Nothing happens.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: No signal. Nine percent battery.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: Down in the lobby, the night guard is watching the game.
"Hello?! Can anybody hear me?"
beats.head: shake

beats.caption: Your voice just bounces back.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: You look at the hatch. You think about climbing out.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: Don't. Climbing out is how people get hurt.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: So you sit down. And wait.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: Saturday morning. The tower is empty.
Your phone dies.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: You're thirsty. But you won't run out of air.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: Elevators aren't airtight. Air keeps coming in.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: Your mom calls. Again. And again.

voices.text: He's not picking up. That's not like him.

beats.caption: Sunday. You've counted every bolt in the wall.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: In 1999, a man in New York was stuck like this. For 41 hours.
A camera was on him the whole time. Nobody looked.
Then, a voice.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: The doors open. Light.
beats.head: breathe

beats.caption: Monday morning, you take the stairs.
beats.head: walk
